title: Greedy Best-First: Faster Routes in Dublin Streets
description: Watch Greedy Best-First race across a real street-map graph, always expanding the node that looks closest to the goal. It’s quick and visually satisfying—but can be shortsighted when the heuristic misleads.
ig_caption:
🚦 Dublin (Ranelagh) street graph, but make it a brainy maze. 

🧠 Greedy Best-First works by always choosing the next node with the smallest heuristic value h(n) (typically straight-line distance to the target), i.e., it greedily chases “what seems closest.” On a real road network modeled as a weighted graph (intersections as nodes, street segments as edges), this often finds a path fast because it prioritizes direction over long-term optimality. 

⚠️ Technical takeaway: Greedy Best-First does *not* guarantee the shortest path like Dijkstra/A*; its efficiency comes from heuristic-driven search, which can backfire near tricky geometry (heuristic traps). 

📍 Want to see how changing the heuristic reshapes the route? Comment your favorite city map challenge, and I’ll generate the next visualization! 🔁✨
